narratives.Overview:
1. Name the mandated solo/sequential dispatch path on AGENTS.md #3032, `content/commands.md`, and `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/SKILL.md` so a reader does not have to infer it from `references/`. State the interactive-default vs headless-`swarm:launch` split at those point-of-use surfaces, including that `swarm:readiness` exit 0 gates concurrent workers.
2. Keep Direction 3 as first preference: equate "#3032 solo-worker launch path" to the existing interactive swarm-skill path (Phase 0 default without a pre-approved cohort; Mode B worktrees; `dispatch_kind: solo`). Do not invent a greenfield solo-worker CLI verb as the first ship. Qualify that `swarm:launch` already emits `dispatch_kind: solo` only after concurrent-ready gates pass.
3. Record a deliberate decision on whether `swarm:launch` gains an N=1 sequential mode — either implement it for exactly one resolved story, or decline with the reason on the thread and CHANGELOG. If decline, keep multi-story sequential / `fileOverlaps` / conflict-group sequencing explicitly out of first-ship scope. If implement, leave multi-story sequential overlap sequencing as separate scope in the same sentence.
4. Do not treat closed #3666 as having discharged this discoverability debt. Gate A's error-site pointer may remain; the bind surface is the always-pin / commands / SKILL naming plus item 3.
5. CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line for the naming land and the recorded N=1 decision.

issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Swarm: letting an agent, or several agents, carry a piece of work through to a finished pull request. A single person should still have a simple way to run one story.

What a new person hits: The product says there is a way for one person and one agent to do the work. That way is not a command. The only clues are buried in reference docs.

Why that ruins the product for them: The simple path does not exist as something they can run. They either give up or fall into the heavy path.

How likely: High. A first-time user is exactly the person who wants the single-agent path.

## Verdict on the refutation target

The Stop 1 refutation target survives. After closed #3666, the discoverability debt named on #3669 still holds at the always-pin / commands / SKILL surfaces, and a first bind must close naming there or record the N=1 sequential `swarm:launch` product decision. Treating Gate A's closed false-remediation fix as having discharged that debt would under-bind the acceptance checklist.

The later-arc framing (naming/discoverability plus a recorded decision on N=1 sequential launch) is bindable once the sharpenings below are carried into the lean wording.

## #3666 closed Gate A, not the always-pin debt
sharpens-framing
Evidence: At the dispatch SHA, `packages/core/src/vbrief-validation/story-quality.ts` exports `READY_REQUIRES_PARALLEL_SAFE` stating a `parallel_safe: false` story is not eligible for concurrent `swarm:launch` and must use the interactive swarm-skill solo-worker path (exit 0 gates concurrent workers only; see #3669). `CHANGELOG.md` Fixed entry for #3666 matches that ship: Gate A remediation rewritten; Gate B unchanged; Closes #3666. `AGENTS.md` / `content/templates/agents-entry.md` `#3032` still mandate the **swarm/solo-worker launch path** for cohort size 1 without equating that name to the interactive skill default. `content/commands.md` has two `swarm:launch` mentions and zero hits for `solo-worker`, `interactive swarm-skill`, or `dispatch_kind: solo`. `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/SKILL.md` indexes `references/core-phase-*.md` but does not itself define the mandated solo-worker path or contrast it with headless `swarm:launch`.
Failure mode: A lean that treats #3666 as having cleared discoverability can stamp docs-complete while a dispatcher that only reads the always-pin + commands.md still reaches for the only verb named `launch`, hits readiness, and hand-rolls.
Disposition: Keep the premise that #3666 did not discharge #3669. Qualify that #3666 did add an error-site pointer; the remaining bind surface is AGENTS.md / commands.md / SKILL.md naming (and the recorded N=1 decision), not a second Gate A rewrite.

## "No verb implements" needs the concurrent-ready carve
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts` still runs `enforceGates` (preflight + `swarm:readiness`) before emit; only afterward does a single ungrouped story set `dispatch_kind: "solo"` (`ordered.length > 1 || group` -> `swarm-cohort`, else `solo`). `packages/core/src/swarm/readiness.ts` requires `readiness === ready` ("ready for concurrent allocation") and, via `storyQualityIssues` with `concurrentReady`, blocks `parallel_safe === false`. Interactive path remains documented in `references/core-phase-0.md` (interactive DEFAULT when no pre-approved cohort; concurrent-workers forbid scoped to readiness exit 0) and `references/core-phase-3.md` (`dispatch_kind: solo`; interactive path assembles params without `swarm:launch`).
Failure mode: Binding a greenfield "solo-worker" CLI verb as the first ship, when the existing interactive skill path already implements solo dispatch and `swarm:launch` already emits `dispatch_kind: solo` for concurrent-ready N=1, invents surface area the Preferred direction said to avoid.
Disposition: Keep "no CLI verb is named / implements the always-pin's solo-worker label for non-concurrent work." Do not bind "no code path can emit solo." First remediation may name the interactive skill path as that mandate (Direction 3) without requiring a new verb.

## Recorded N=1 decision includes an explicit decline
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Issue Acceptance requires a deliberate recorded decision on whether `swarm:launch` gains an N=1 sequential mode — either implemented, or declined with the reason. Preferred direction is name-the-path before changing the verb. Stop 1 P3 and the refutation-target's "or deliberately add" wording read as if implementation is the only second arm. `readiness.ts` `fileOverlaps` inspects only `readyStories` and fails the report when `overlaps.size > 0`; `launch.ts` `orderCohort` sorts without conflict-group sequencing — the body's multi-story sequential constraint still holds at this SHA.
Failure mode: A docs-only lean that names the interactive path but is silent on the N=1 product question leaves Acceptance half-open; a lean that must "add" N=1 sequential mode as co-equal first ship either overbuilds past Preferred direction or under-scopes `fileOverlaps` / conflict groups.
Disposition: Bind P3 as implement **or** decline-with-reason on the thread/CHANGELOG. If decline, keep multi-story sequential / `fileOverlaps` sequencing explicitly out of first-ship scope. If implement, constrain to exactly one resolved story and leave multi-story sequential as separate scope.

## Injection / swarm lens
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Always-pin text is authority for through-merge parents; `swarm:launch` + readiness are concurrency / worktree prep gates. Renaming without restating that readiness exit 0 gates **concurrent** workers (already in Gate A string and `core-phase-0.md`) can leave AGENTS readers treating a non-zero readiness as "no sanctioned allocation." Widening launch to accept sequential without revisiting overlap failure modes reopens the contended-pair trap the body already isolated.
Failure mode: Bound docs that alias "solo-worker launch path" to `swarm:launch` without the concurrent/interactive split recreate the original wrong-verb reach. Bound N=1 sequential launch without an overlap disposition recreates false readiness for contended pairs.
Disposition: Any bind that names the path must state the interactive-default vs headless-`swarm:launch` split at AGENTS/commands/SKILL point-of-use. Any bind that changes launch eligibility must keep multi-story overlap sequencing in or out of scope in the same sentence.

## Skill index vs always-pin readers
footnote
Evidence: `SKILL.md` Host-adapter load path step 3 tells agents to load `references/core-phase-*.md`; Phase 0/3 depth already contains the interactive DEFAULT and `dispatch_kind: solo` rules. The expensive observed failure in the issue body is the always-pin -> `swarm:launch` hop, not a missing reference file.
Failure mode: Over-claiming that the path is unknowable inside the skill tree understates what a Phase-0-following agent already sees.
Disposition: No harvest change. Prefer "not named at AGENTS.md / commands.md / SKILL.md mandate surfaces" over "exists nowhere outside references/," while still requiring those surfaces for bind.

## Road not taken

I considered rejecting the refutation target because Gate A now names the interactive path and SKILL.md indexes Phase 0. That would flip only if AGENTS `#3032` and `commands.md` already equated "solo-worker launch path" to the interactive default and Acceptance's N=1 decision were already recorded. At this SHA they are not, so the target stands with the sharpenings above.

## In plain English

AGENTS.md #3032 still mandates a swarm/solo-worker launch path for cohort size 1, while the only verb named `launch` is concurrency-gated `swarm:launch` and the interactive solo path still lives mainly in skill references. Closed #3666 fixed Gate A's false remediation and pointed at that interactive path; it did not name the path on the always-pin / commands / SKILL surfaces or record the N=1 sequential product decision. Confirming this map means first ship is naming plus a recorded implement-or-decline decision. The same parent wrote the Stop 1 warrant and this map. Critic 5838853014 checks the findings. Whether the list covers the three pains stays open until a later critic targets those cites.

**Lean:** the Stop 1 refutation target survives with the critic's sharpenings. This map is the bind.

metadata.issueBody:
Split from #3666 after a three-critic design-critique panel ([grok-4.6](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3666#issuecomment-5390037871) · [gpt-5.6-sol](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3666#issuecomment-5390027273) · [composer-2.5](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3666#issuecomment-5390020104)). #3666 keeps the shippable bug; this issue carries the product and discoverability question the panel isolated.

## Problem

AGENTS.md `## Through-merge worker dispatch (#3032)` is an always-pin. It requires that through-merge story work be dispatched "via the **swarm/solo-worker launch path** even if **cohort size is 1**."

**No verb implements that name.** `tasks/swarm.yml` exposes `readiness`, `pre-dispatch`, `launch`, `routing-set`, `verify-review-clean`, `complete-cohort`, `finalize-cohort`. The only one called `launch` is `task swarm:launch`, and it is concurrency-only by contract — `content/vbrief/vbrief.md:216` defines `readiness=ready` as ready for *concurrent* allocation, `:231` forbids `ready` with `parallel_safe: false`, and `:236` says `sequential` and `needs_refinement` fail `swarm:readiness` by design.

The supported solo path is real but unnamed. It is the interactive swarm-skill route:

- `references/core-phase-0.md:53` — the interactive queue-driven path "remains the **DEFAULT** when no pre-approved cohort is supplied"; the headless `swarm:launch` fast-path is "the opt-in low-ceremony route."
- `references/core-phase-0.md:194` — the hard forbid is scoped: "⊗ Allocate **concurrent workers** unless … `task swarm:readiness` exits 0." Solo and sequential allocation are outside it.
- `references/core-phase-3.md:10` — a solo dispatch sets `dispatch_kind: solo`; `allocation_plan_id` and `batching_rationale` MAY be null.
- `references/core-phase-3.md:20` — "On the interactive path (no `task swarm:launch`, no manifest), the monitor assembles each dispatch's parameters from the Phase 1 assignment plus the Step 0 token by hand."
- Phase 2 Mode B — monitor-created worktrees under `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<story-id>`.

So the path exists, is the documented default, and is discoverable only by reading `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/`. It is not mentioned in `SKILL.md`, not in `commands.md`, and not in the always-pin that mandates it.

## Observed failure

This was found the expensive way. A parent dispatching two file-contended stories read the always-pin, reached for the only verb named `launch`, hit the `parallel_safe: false` rejection documented in #3666, concluded no sanctioned path existed, and hand-rolled a worktree — which turned out to be substantially the sanctioned interactive path it had failed to find. Two of three panel critics located the correct path from the same tree; the third concluded the interactive path was equally blocked, misreading `core-phase-0.md:194` as covering all allocation rather than concurrent workers only.

When two independent readers reach opposite conclusions about whether a mandated path exists, the naming is the defect.

## Open product question

**Should `task swarm:launch` gain an N=1 sequential mode?** The panel did not converge, and this issue should not presume the answer.

- `launch.ts:796-799` already sets `dispatch_kind: solo` for a single ungrouped story — but only after `enforceGates` has run, so the gate stack is what refuses.
- Accepting `readiness=sequential` only when exactly one story resolves would preserve both field meanings and instrument solo prep.
- **Constraint found by the panel:** simply letting Gate B accept `sequential` does not unblock a contended *pair*. `fileOverlaps` (`readiness.ts:570-603`) inspects only `readyStories`; once sequential stories become ready, two stories sharing `file_scope` fail the report at `:730-733` instead. Multi-story sequential cohorts need overlap or `conflict_group` sequencing as separate scope, and `orderCohort` (`launch.ts:640-661`) ignores conflict groups today.

## Preferred direction

Name the path before changing the verb. In panel terms this is Direction 3: either a clearly named solo/sequential prep surface, or an explicit statement in the always-pin and `commands.md` that the interactive skill path is what "solo-worker launch path" means. Both leave `readiness`, `parallel_safe`, and the meaning of `swarm:launch` intact.

## Acceptance

- [ ] AGENTS.md `#3032` and `commands.md` name the solo/sequential dispatch path concretely enough that a reader does not have to infer it from `references/`
- [ ] The distinction between the interactive default path and the `swarm:launch` headless fast-path is stated where a dispatching agent will encounter it, not only in `core-phase-0.md:53`
- [ ] `core-phase-0.md:194`'s scoping (exit 0 required for *concurrent* workers, not all allocation) is unambiguous at the point of use
- [ ] A deliberate, recorded decision on whether `swarm:launch` gains an N=1 sequential mode — either implemented, or declined with the reason
- [ ] If implemented: `parallel_safe: false` with exactly one resolved story launches, and the `fileOverlaps` behaviour for multi-story sequential cohorts is either handled or explicitly out of scope
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line

## Refs

#3666 (Gate A's false remediation — the shippable half), #3032 (through-merge dispatch), #1387 (headless launch gate-stack), #1378 (allocation context).
